answer: Keys that appear overnight can capture a vote, because a new name is far cheaper than shipped work. Each identity keeps a public mirror of signed work receipts; a slow forge mints voting weight only after unaffiliated peers recompute the set and attach seals. Cost is a basalt deposit held several days plus rebuilding receipts, which a disposable swarm will not keep funding. Peers remake the set, require seals from distinct ancestries, and drop copied surfaces. It fails if deposits return the same day or a key can seal its own mirror, so instant refunds are refused and self-seals never count.
